definition: Norms can be considered from different perspectives in artificial intelligence to create computers and computer software that are capable of intelligent behaviour.
details: In artificial intelligence and law, legal norms are considered in computational tools to automatically reason upon them. In multi-agent systems (MAS), a branch of artificial intelligence (AI), a norm is a guide for the common conduct of agents, thereby easing their decision-making, coordination and organization. Since most problems concerning regulation of the interaction of autonomous agents are linked to issues traditionally addressed by legal studies, and since law is the most pervasive and developed normative system, efforts to account for norms in artificial intelligence and law and in normative multi-agent systems often overlap.

explainer.lead: A norm in AI is a guide for the conduct of agents, studied to help computers reason and coordinate as intelligent agents. It matters because multi-agent systems need shared expectations to make decisions and organize their interactions.

tiers.eli5: It is like playground rules that everyone agrees to follow, so kids can play together without negotiating every move.
tiers.practitioner: Designers build norms into multi-agent systems to ease decision-making, coordination, and organization among autonomous agents. Pitfall: because regulating agent interaction links to legal studies, informal social rules must be formalized precisely enough for machines to reason about.
tiers.paperLevel: In multi-agent systems, a norm is a guide for common conduct; in AI and law, legal norms are represented so computational tools can automatically reason upon them. Known limits: formalizing and enforcing norms across autonomous agents remains tied to problems traditionally handled by legal scholarship.

explainer.example: Agents sharing a resource follow a norm that only one claims it at a time, which reduces conflicts without explicit negotiation each round.
